biggest_gap.title: The new partition check in ./erp verify fails at random, so the one command can fail from a clean clone before any .NET test runs
biggest_gap.detail: This round's build/verify-inside.sh lists the tests twice with 'dotnet test Erp.slnx --list-tests' (once for the whole suite, once as the 'projects' group) and diffs the two lists against the groups. A solution listing runs the test projects at the same time, and their lines interleave: two test names end up on one line, or a line is cut. When the two listings interleave differently, the diff fails, and the whole .NET stage exits 1 with 'The test groups are not every test exactly once'. No test has run at that point. This happened in my first clean-clone verify, at a load of up to 122 with three verify slots shared. I then reproduced it with no plant involved: 12 listings of one unchanged build at load 60 to 75 gave lines naming two tests in 5 of the 12 (1, 19, 1, 1 and 5 such lines). So under the normal three-slot load the dotnet stage can fail on most runs, whatever the product's code. My second run happened to get two clean listings and then passed all 1,129 .NET tests. The check itself is a good idea (every test exactly once), but it must not depend on how parallel output interleaves. Fix suggestions for the builder: list one project at a time (-m:1, or loop over the test csproj files), or compare test names taken from the trx results. Second point: in the shared three-slot setting, the parallel groups did not shorten the stage. It took 11,184 s, against r19's 10,374 s quiet alone run, and its counted processor time was 23,744 s for dotnet alone (27,187 s in all against the 23,300 s maximum, at load peaks near 100 with my plant run beside it). G1ListVolume, scheduled after the self-test groups, ran alone at the tail.
